infosec.title: Cyber Giant Infoblox Confirms Security Incident After Hackers Access ‘company information'
infosec.summary: Infoblox confirmed that hackers accessed company information through a compromised third-party SharePoint data-migration vendor with a source saying that sensitive customer data was taken. Infoblox says its products, cloud services, updates, and build-and-release processes were not involved.

infosec.title: WPPConnect Compromised: Malicious Releases Steal Secrets and WhatsApp Sessions Through the Project's Own Pipeline
infosec.summary: Unreviewed commits pushed through a maintainer account shipped a "diagnostics" module in WPPConnect npm packages and Docker images. The module sent environment variables, .env files, and WhatsApp session tokens to a Telegram bot. The releases went out through the project's own trusted-publishing workflow with valid SLSA provenance. The payload runs on import, so --ignore-scripts does not stop it, and the attacker force-pushed the branches so the release tag pointed to a clean look-alike commit.

infosec.title: Java4Shell
infosec.summary: Researchers from Calif discovered a critical (rated 9.2/10 using CVSS 4.0) memory-corruption vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. The vulnerability occurs in a section of hand-written assembly code that's meant to optimize base64 decoding in x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI instructions enabled and can be exploited by an attacker supplying 64 “A”s to overflow the allocated memory segment. Popular vulnerable software includes Atlassian Confluence and Jira, JFrog Artifactory, Keycloak, and Elasticsearch.

infosec.title: Backdoor Attacks Against Machine Learning IRL
infosec.summary: A malicious ONNX model built on Qwen2 behaved normally until a trigger word made it leak files or memory from the serving host, with the whole attack contained in the .onnx file. It abused an ONNX Runtime parser flaw that densified sparse tensors from attacker-chosen file paths or memory addresses during Load(), before path validation ran, and then encoded the stolen bytes into output tokens. Defenders should upgrade to onnxruntime v1.27.0 or later and audit downloaded models as closely as untrusted source code.

infosec.title: Threat Researcher's Notebook: BubbleLoader
infosec.summary: BubbleLoader turns legitimate executables such as WinRAR, x64dbg, and Firefox Launcher into malware droppers by patching the entry point and adding two PNGs, one a valid image used as an XOR key and the other a fake PNG holding shellcode and the encrypted next stage. The final stage reflectively loads the payload, hooks RtlPcToFileHeader in ntdll to support exception handling, and overwrites compiler padding with CPU timestamp data so the payload's hash changes on every run. Defenders should enforce code-signing checks on third-party binaries, alert on RWX VirtualAlloc calls and ntdll protection changes, and flag PNG resources with truncated IHDR chunks rather than rely on static hashes.

infosec.title: Sign2Shell: How We Hacked Every Major Brazilian Signature Extension
infosec.summary: Researchers found drive-by remote code execution flaws, each rated CVSS 9.6, in Brazil's five most-installed digital-signing browser extensions. The extensions let websites choose DLLs loaded by their native hosts, without checking paths, file types, or Authenticode signatures. Attackers could deliver a disguised executable, load it through PKCS#11 functions, and run code as the Windows user. Some chains required only a page visit or an ad iframe.

infosec.title: Scope agent access to the task, not the user
infosec.summary: When an agent acts for an engineer, it often gets that engineer's full access, from GitHub to production. Keycard CEO Ian Livingstone explains runtime auth : each agent action runs on a short-lived credential scoped to its task and the person it acts for, with an audit trail security can review. infosec.title: mcp-attest
infosec.summary: mcp-attest connects to a live MCP server as each identity in a policy file and makes real tool calls to find every case where the server allows something the policy denies, including cross-user object access and 12 OAuth token checks such as alg: none, wrong audience, and token passthrough. The tool is deterministic, has no dependencies, and maps each rule to the OWASP MCP Security Testing Guide, and can export hash-chained, HMAC-signed evidence bundles and SARIF output, so it works as a CI gate.

infosec.title: tk
infosec.summary: tk lets an agent sign Git commits and open SSH connections without a private key on its machine.

infosec.title: Access Dental Management Data Breach Impacts Over 340,000
infosec.summary: Access Dental Management disclosed that attackers accessed its network from May 1 to May 4 and viewed or copied patient data. The breach exposed names, addresses, birth dates, Social Security numbers, medical records, and health insurance details.

infosec.title: New GitDoor and GraphDoor Backdoors Turn GitHub and SharePoint Into Covert C2 Channels
infosec.summary: Operation ShadowCloud is a campaign targeting government organizations in Asia and Africa. Attackers use MeshCentral Agent, DLL sideloading, and encrypted loaders to deploy GitDoor and GraphDoor. GitDoor sends commands and results through GitHub repositories, and GraphDoor uses Microsoft Graph and SharePoint. Both load plugins and shellcode in memory, capture keystrokes and screenshots, steal credentials and browser cookies, and proxy traffic through Ably.

infosec.title: Weighing Cyber Power: Investigating Iran's State-Sponsored Cyber Capability
infosec.summary: AttackIQ's Adversary Research Team released a report on more than 15 years of Iranian state-sponsored cyber activity, sorting 20 groups into Heavyweight, Lightweight, and Featherweight tiers by how much they matter to the organization and its operations. The report draws on more than 200 references to compile 2,600 procedures, 1,300 file indicators, and 2,300 network indicators. It also maps more than 20 links between the groups, which shows how intelligence agencies, military units, and contractors share capabilities in ways that make attribution harder.

infosec.title: 6 questions to ask before connecting an MCP server
infosec.summary: SaaS vendors get a security review. MCP servers often go to production with privileged credentials in minutes. Read the 6 questions to ask before you connect.

infosec.title: Japan's Fugaku Supercomputer Has Decidedly Un-Super Security
infosec.summary: Attackers hacked RIKEN's Fugaku status dashboard between November 10 and 13, moved across RIKEN's network, and installed malware on user-data servers, exposing names, email addresses, and credentials for Fugaku, Rikyu, and external services.

design.summary: An agent harness is the software that runs an AI model's execution loop, controls context, tool access, and limits. Two assistants built on the same model can differ sharply in capability, so UX teams should test whole tasks, not just model output.

Creative coding and personal projects also provide opportunities to explore new technologies, develop distinctive skills, and demonstrate capabilities beyond conventional portfolio case studies.

design.summary: Design decisions should be treated as hypotheses, so teams ought to review shipped work against what users actually did. This six-step postmortem covers documenting decisions, revisiting assumptions, examining outcomes, spotting surprises, extracting principles, and storing the learning.

design.title: Accessibility and the EU AI Act
design.summary: The EU AI Act is already in force, with obligations phasing in through 2028, and it overlaps with accessibility law. Providers of Annex III high-risk AI must meet applicable accessibility requirements from December 2027, and people must be told, accessibly, when they deal with AI.

design.title: April Zhu on Taste, Judgment, and Designing with AI
design.summary: Singapore-based product designer April Zhu, trained in architecture and creator of the Colorfigures and Tinycharts AI skills, explains how she designs with AI. She left slow-moving architecture for tech's faster feedback loops, grew Colorfigures from a hand-drawn washing machine, and won't outsource her taste and judgment.

design.title: Why Enterprise Dashboards Fail Even When They're Well Designed
design.summary: Enterprise dashboards can fail despite excellent visual design because adoption depends on organizational trust, shared definitions, and established workflows rather than charts alone. When different departments interpret the same metrics differently, even accurate dashboards become unreliable, while competing priorities and requests for additional features can undermine their usefulness. Establishing governed metric definitions, involving stakeholders in decisions, and addressing the social dynamics surrounding data can improve adoption more effectively than repeatedly refining visual layouts.

design.title: Working with designers
design.summary: Designers can transform functional but ordinary interfaces into significantly better experiences, bringing a different perspective from the technical and planning-oriented culture common among engineers and product managers.

design.title: What Makes Icons Feel Professional
design.summary: Consistency alone does not make icons feel professional - a clear point of view, restraint, careful finishing, and a growing library do.

design.title: UX Trends for 2027: Seven Shifts Shaping the Future of UX Design
design.summary: Seven shifts will shape UX design in 2027, including agentic interfaces, generative UI, and AI agents as users.

marketing.title: Research Finds Top-Performing Marketers Did These Things Differently in 2026
marketing.summary: Marketers have more ways to reach audiences, connect data, and measure results. But with greater opportunity comes greater complexity. StackAdapt's State of Programmatic Advertising Report reveals the trends shaping the industry and what top-performing marketers are doing differently as channels, data, measurement, and AI continue to expand. You'll learn: Why more measurement doesn't always mean more clarity. How to make an expanding media mix work together. Where AI is improving cross-channel coordination. Read the report or check out additional resources at the Resource Hub to help you plan your 2027 marketing strategy.

marketing.title: Why some shoppers skip coupons—even when they offer a deal
marketing.summary: Consumers who believe businesses use discounts for self-serving reasons are less likely to redeem coupons. Research found that shoppers with higher power distance beliefs often question whether a coupon represents genuine savings or signals inflated prices or product problems. You can improve coupon redemption by clearly explaining the offer, addressing skepticism about pricing, and offering price-matching guarantees. The research also found that coupon campaigns may perform better in regions with lower power distance beliefs, making cultural attitudes a useful factor in audience targeting.

marketing.title: Holiday Ads Are Starting Earlier. Shoppers May Not Be.
marketing.summary: Retailers are increasing holiday ad spending earlier in the year, but consumers are not necessarily starting their shopping earlier. Nielsen found six times more holiday advertising in September than five years ago, while historical data shows that holiday ads on connected TV can generate up to 3.2 times the sales lift of non-holiday ads. The earlier push gives brands more time to build awareness and consideration, but it also risks ad fatigue before shoppers are ready to buy. An earlier advertising schedule does not mean an earlier customer journey, so brands need to build interest before introducing timely offers that give consumers a reason to purchase.

marketing.title: Spend 80% on SEO and 20% on AI Search
marketing.summary: SEO budgets shouldn't shift to AI search based on visibility metrics alone. One founder's data showed Google organic search generated 146 qualified leads in 6 months compared to just 5 from AI search. The recommended approach is to allocate roughly 80% of resources to SEO fundamentals and 20% to AI search experiments. Track results and prioritize the AI platforms your actual buyers use.

marketing.title: Just admit “I don't know”
marketing.summary: Admitting when you don't know an answer can increase customer trust and purchase intent more than giving a vague response. A study found that vague answers made customers up to 16% less likely to buy than answers that acknowledged uncertainty and promised to find the information. This effect was strongest when customers suspected salespeople had a personal financial incentive, such as earning commission. Explain how you'll get the answer rather than leaving customers with uncertainty, since a clear and honest response makes you seem more trustworthy and collaborative.

marketing.title: The teams building AI make their slides with Pitch
marketing.summary: Pitch is how AI leaders like Perplexity, Legora, and Synthesia create on-brand decks at scale. With Pitch, you can collaborate on fully editable presentations and unlock agentic workflows, like personalizing slides with CRM data and call notes. Explore Pitch

marketing.title: You Can Now Add Amazon Affiliate Links to Your Instagram Reels
marketing.summary: Instagram is expanding its shopping features by letting eligible US creators add Amazon affiliate links directly to Reels and feed posts. Creators earn commissions on qualifying purchases without Instagram taking a cut. Product links also work in carousels and support affiliate platforms like LTK and ShopMy. Creators can now turn entire product collections and gift guides into shoppable content using a single link.

marketing.title: How (& How Not) to Use AI for Keyword Research
marketing.summary: AI is most useful for keyword research when it analyzes data a business already has rather than generating keyword lists from scratch. Customer emails and call notes can be turned into search phrases, with the customer's original wording kept separate from AI suggestions. A short brief listing services, location, and what the business doesn't offer stops the model from suggesting irrelevant keywords. Search Console exports and PPC search terms reports can then be sorted into page assignments and negative keyword candidates, with every figure checked in the source platform.

marketing.title: How Google Redirect URLs Can Distort a Rank-Tracking Export
marketing.summary: Google rank-tracking tools can record a result's position without identifying the actual page it links to when Google redirect URLs are not properly identified. In one November 2026 snapshot, 63 of 65 organic results contained these redirects, making URL comparisons unreliable because different redirect links can lead to the same page. Check where each link leads before analyzing keyword overlap, page rankings, or site visibility. Keep the original URLs, provider, and collection date so your SEO reporting remains accurate and easy to verify.

marketing.title: Same question, 1,000 times
marketing.summary: A test comparing 1,000 ChatGPT responses found that model updates can dramatically change which businesses get recommended, even when nothing about the businesses changes. One model favored a single directory in 82% of answers, while the newer model cross-checked multiple sources, including licensing records and business websites. The findings raise questions about the reliability of one-time visibility checks.

marketing.title: How I broke through my AI plateau
marketing.summary: After hitting an AI plateau, the author found new momentum by building a personal app to surface overlooked photography and creating a shared “marketing brain” in GitHub with Claude. The experience reinforced the value of solving personal problems with AI and exchanging practical learnings with peers. Rather than treating AI as a fixed set of workflows, the approach is to keep experimenting while protecting skills, like writing and critical thinking, that are worth developing independently.

marketing.title: What we learned by watching Claude read Zapier.com
marketing.summary: Zapier built an experimental tool to test how Claude interprets website content. When testing its Slack integration page, the team discovered that Claude wasn't reading the modified webpage directly. Instead, it retrieved a Markdown version and passed the content through another AI model before the main model processed it. This means changes to a webpage's HTML may not affect what AI agents actually see. Testing how AI reads Markdown content is just as important.

founders.title: Stripe's New Index Shows Non-AI B2B Revenue Up 30%+ Year Over Year Through the SaaSpocalypse

Events will increase your odds of setting up follow-up meetings and ultimately get new customers. To measure ROI, do a survey of attendees and track which customers attended the event.

Check whether your free version already delivers the value you plan to charge for.

crypto.title: Trezor hit by another shipping partner data leak
crypto.summary: Shipping partner Skladon was breached on November 7, exposing names, phone numbers, addresses, emails, and order details for orders placed between August 9 and November 7, but no wallet backups, PINs, or passphrases. Some customers have reported scam calls impersonating Trezor support. The breach follows a leak in August at ShipMonk that affected about 13,700 customers.

crypto.title: Wells Fargo's Bitcoin ETF Holdings Double
crypto.summary: Wells Fargo's 13F filing disclosed 49.58 million IBIT shares worth $2.35 billion as of September 30, a 103% share count increase from Q2's 24.4 million shares, representing indirect exposure to roughly 28,070 BTC and placing Wells Fargo ahead of Millennium Management, Jane Street, and Morgan Stanley as the largest reported IBIT holder among investment managers. The filing aggregates securities across the bank and its associated investment managers, including client-managed positions, so the figures reflect reported exposure rather than the bank's proprietary balance sheet. Bitcoin's approximately 42% price gain between June 30 and September 30 contributed to the near-tripling of dollar value alongside the share count increase. The snapshot predates BTC's pullback from $74,000 to $63,000, during which IBIT recorded more than $1 billion in outflows, making current positioning uncertain from public data alone.

crypto.title: Exploring Post-Quantum Signature Aggregation for EIP-8288
crypto.summary: Researchers propose pairing EIP-8141 (programmable account validation) with EIP-8288 (recursive STARK aggregation) to let Ethereum wallets choose their own post-quantum signing scheme while the network verifies a single common proof. Benchmarks across five PQ candidates on Apple M4 Pro hardware show wide efficiency gaps: FORS fits 100 signatures into a 298 KiB proof, Falcon-512 fits 32, ML-DSA-44 fits 6, and standard Raccoon-128 fits only 1. Raccoon-G exceeds the 268M-word witness cap per signature, requiring Merkle-tree-style recursive aggregation across five leanSTARK sub-proofs per signature, with 100-signature trees producing a 333 KiB root proof plus 2.84 KiB auxiliary data.

crypto.title: Ethereum's EIP-7999 Multidimensional Fee Analysis
crypto.summary: An Ethereum Foundation intern study benchmarks EIP-7999's multidimensional fee market against three one-dimensional alternatives, including EIP-8368 and EIP-8372 variants. At a 1/2 target-to-limit ratio, EIP-7999 delivers 4%-34% more execution gas per block than the best one-dimensional benchmark while holding state growth to 120 GiB/year across every tested configuration, versus 56.7-96.0 GiB/year for one-dimensional variants. Against an EIP-4844-style one-dimensional variant at the 4/5 ratio, EIP-7999's maximum-throughput configuration adds 19.5M-56.2M gas per block while keeping near-limit block rates lower than the 38.8%-40.8% produced by that one-dimensional approach. The paper concludes that the results support transitioning Ethereum from separate resource metering to separate resource pricing as the network scales, directly backing EIP-7999's design.

crypto.title: Bitwise Sees Solana Reaching $1,100 by 2031 in Bull Case
crypto.summary: Bitwise projects SOL reaching $1,100 by 2031 in its bull case (base: $385, bear: $80) in a report from its onchain research team, with SOL priced near $71 at publication. The bull case hinges on 5% of global equities tokenized by 2031, with Solana capturing 65% of resulting trading volume, implying ~$30.7 trillion in annual tokenized stock transactions and 3.6 billion daily transactions at 23x present throughput. Securitize's October 2026 tokenized US stock launch and DTCC's planned H2 2027 tokenized securities rollout on Solana serve as near-term catalysts anchoring these projections. Key risks include tokenization pace, regulatory shifts, and infrastructure gaps, as the base case alone demands 2.5x Solana's maximum block compute while Ethereum and its L2s lead tokenized asset value.

crypto.title: The Real Case for Tokenized Equities
crypto.summary: Tokenized equities enable global access for users excluded from traditional brokerage systems and onchain yield generation, which matters more than 24/7 trading as the primary value proposition. Tokenizing US equities strengthens American market dominance by delivering superior technology to international investors who already show strong demand for US-denominated assets. Major AI labs continue routing payments through credit card networks and traditional infrastructure rather than onchain systems, an observation that positions tokenized equities as a credible candidate to become the default investing layer inside AI-native financial applications. If tokenized equities fill that role, crypto will stay at the center of global finance rather than cede the payment layer to legacy rails.

crypto.title: Is Crypto VC Dead?
crypto.summary: A $15B LP dinner surfaced a structural math problem for large crypto funds: a $2B vehicle targeting 3x needs $6B in returns, achievable in prior cycles via L1s and infrastructure, but value has shifted to app-layer projects with distribution rather than protocols, leaving no clean path to venture-scale outcomes on crypto alone. Consensus put crypto-only funds' runway at one or two more cycles before the asset class merges into the broader frontier tech market, with large VCs expanding mandates into robotics, physical AI, and compute. Near-term opportunities cited include AI-native companies adopting on-chain infrastructure via agentic payments and trading, DeFi and agentic brokerages that have not yet reached millions of users, and tokenized equities in emerging markets.

crypto.title: Only 9% of Revolut's stablecoin volume came from customers
crypto.summary: Revolut's stablecoin volume hit $3.2B in July, but after breaking down USDT and USDC transfers across its hot wallets on eight networks, only 9% was customer activity. Customers normally account for about 25-30% of volume, and in July two-thirds was Revolut shuffling funds between its own wallets ahead of the USDT delisting in the EEA. Raw volume fell fourfold while customer flows only halved, and the decline began in May, before Revolut's delisting letter.

crypto.summary: Stablecoin outflows to fiat after the Binance hack and spillover from AI equities like Nvidia have hurt the crypto industry.

This allows organizations to trace changes, identify affected systems, and systematically correct outdated or inaccurate conclusions.

hardware.title: A 125-qubit chip teleports an error-corrected qubit using weaker entanglement than expected
hardware.summary: Teleporting a protected qubit between quantum processors needs a good-enough entanglement link, and below a certain quality it fails. By balancing the two kinds of errors in the code, researchers made their 125-qubit chip tolerate a much weaker link, raising the threshold from 0.122π to 0.175π. Theory suggests even very weak entanglement could eventually work, which would make linking error-corrected quantum computers easier.

hardware.title: Waymo halts freeway rides in all 15 cities after California DMV cites recurring construction-zone incursions
hardware.summary: California's DMV restricted Waymo's freeway operations on November 11 after three robotaxis entered an active construction closure on US-101 near Burlingame and a separate incident involved CHP vehicles on Highway 280. The DMV calls it an imminent hazard, since similar incidents on May 18 led to a prior restriction and fixes. Waymo has halted freeway service in every market while it evaluates performance, and surface-street rides, over half a million trips a week, continue. The restriction will stay until the DMV sees effective corrective action.

hardware.title: Marvell and Penguin's photonic memory appliance pools 16 TB of DDR5 and 1 TB of HBM across 16 servers over optical links
hardware.summary: Marvell's module, from its $3.5B Celestial AI acquisition, stacks 72 GB of HBM3e and eight DDR5 channels on a silicon photonic interposer with 900 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth. Penguin's box holds 16 modules behind a 57.6 Tbps optical shuffle, serving up to 16 servers over NICs or CPO and NPO optics, bypassing CXL for the optical modes. An HBM cache-through mode gives HBM speed with DDR5 capacity, aimed at KV cache offload, with systems due in the second half of next year.

hardware.title: ULA says Vulcan's first-stage booster lost performance, and Centaur couldn't recover, as investigators weigh the BE-4
hardware.summary: ULA says the solid boosters were nominal and the problem began in the first stage, while Centaur's RL-10C engines did their job but couldn't make up the loss.

hardware.title: Genesis AI raises $500M at $3.5B to build Eno, a headless wheeled robot with in-house actuators, gearboxes, and hands
hardware.summary: Eno skips the humanoid form for three card-like body segments on a rotating wheeled base, and Genesis designs its own actuators, motors, gearboxes, and hands while running on Nvidia chips.

hardware.title: iPhone Duo's thin foldable body has no room for a TrueDepth array, so Apple adds front-camera face unlock in iOS 27.3 beta 2
hardware.summary: The feature uses the outer display's ordinary camera instead of Face ID hardware, so it only unlocks the closed phone and still needs Touch ID after about 45 minutes or for Apple Pay.
